candidates.text: We hold that it does, but that a mental state of recklessness is sufficient. The State must show that the defendant consciously disregarded a substantial risk
candidates.speaker: Kagan, for the Court
phrases: consciously disregarded a substantial risk that his communications would be viewed as threatening violence

candidates.text: Yet the First Amendment may still demand a subjective mental-state requirement shielding some true threats from liability.
candidates.speaker: Kagan, for the Court
phrases: may still demand a subjective mental-state requirement shielding some true threats from liability

candidates.text: The reality is that recklessness is not grounded in law, but in a Goldilocks judgment: Recklessness is not too much, not too little
candidates.speaker: Barrett, dissenting
phrases: recklessness is not grounded in law, but in a Goldilocks judgment

candidates.text: There is simply no need to reach out in this stalking case to determine whether anything more than recklessness is needed
candidates.speaker: Sotomayor, concurring in part and in the judgment
